summary: Test fixtures opened with Store::open_memory now use owned temporary file-backed WAL stores, so a reader snapshot can coexist with a writer instead of failing immediately on SQLite shared-cache table locks. A tmpfs TMPDIR owns fixture scratch and process-exit leftovers; explicit memory-mode controls use open_shared_memory.

replay.detail: No deployed graph replay or backfill. Test-support fixtures use normal file-backed initialization, including the resource-reference backfill for downstream binaries.

schema.detail: No schema, claim, storage-version or persisted-data changes.

rules.detail: No authority, rules or coordination changes.

compatibility.detail: Production builds exclude both fixture constructors unless test-support is enabled. Fixture stores use the existing file-backed path. Shared-cache behavior remains available explicitly for memory-mode tests. The two IVM examples require test-support.

downtime.detail: No deployment or daemon restart is required for this test-only change.

manual.detail: No operator action. Normally scratch is removed after the last writer or reader owner closes. When TMPDIR is tmpfs, scratch stays beneath it so run cleanup also reclaims process-exit leftovers.

recovery.detail: Revert the test constructor change; no data migration is needed.
